headline: Losses narrow as subscription growth outpaces cost growth
summary_short: Revenue rose 39% year-over-year to $387.1 million as Subscription ARR grew 32% to $1.57 billion, while net loss narrowed to $41.9 million (EPS -$0.21) from $102.1 million a year earlier.
summary_long: Fiscal Q1 2027 revenue (three months ended April 30, 2026) grew 39% y/y to $387.1M, driven by 32% Subscription ARR growth to $1.57B and ~$8.5M of non-recurring Subscription Credit conversions. Gross margin expanded to 81% from 78% on scale, despite higher hosting costs. Operating loss narrowed to $52.6M from $93.1M as revenue outpaced 40% R&D growth (headcount, hosting) and 14% S&M growth; G&A fell 4%. Net loss narrowed to $41.9M ($0.21/share) from $102.1M, helped by higher interest income. Free cash flow rose to $73.6M from $33.3M. Convertible notes ($1.15B, issued June 2025) remain outstanding; no forward guidance appears in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by Subscription ARR growth (+32% y/y to $1.57B) and about $8.5M of non-recurring revenue from customers exercising or forfeiting Subscription Credits.
Subscription gross margin expanded on economies of scale as revenue grew faster than cost of revenue, despite $8.5M higher hosting costs from expanded SaaS adoption.
Loss narrowed as opex grew slower than revenue: R&D +40% (headcount, $9.8M more hosting/software) and S&M +14% (marketing, headcount), while G&A fell 4% on lower stock comp.
Narrowed on the operating-loss improvement plus higher interest income ($15.9M vs $7.7M) and lower interest expense following the 2025 convertible-note refinancing.
Company attributes the improvement to higher sales including timing of renewals, improved operating leverage, and optimizing the capital structure.
Held near the prior year's level (~120%) as expansion from existing customers offset contraction and attrition; no numeric split given.
